sources.title: The Colonic Crypt: Cellular Dynamics and Signaling Pathways in Homeostasis and Cancer
sources.locator: WNT falls progressively up the crypt axis; stem cells show high WNT activity; WNT comes from mesenchyme near the base and not distally; differentiation completes at the crypt top; Frizzled with LRP5/6 is the receptor; a destruction complex of APC, AXIN, CK1A and GSK3B marks beta-catenin for proteasomal degradation and is recruited to the membrane on WNT binding; targets c-MYC, LGR5, cyclin D1; 93 per cent of colorectal cancers carry a pathway mutation, mostly APC; renewal 3-5 days.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the direction and source of the crypt Wnt gradient, the identity of the receptor complex, the composition and action of the destruction complex, the consequence of Wnt binding, the named transcriptional targets, the pathway mutation frequency in colorectal cancer, and the renewal intervals. sources.title: APC controls Wnt-induced beta-catenin destruction complex recruitment in human colonocytes
sources.locator: Destruction complex components including Axin1, GSK-3beta and beta-catenin localised toward Wnt3a-coated beads in 61 to 80 per cent of cells with full-length APC, about 30 per cent with truncated APC, and were abolished where APC was deleted; the authors propose the complex keeps its composition and its beta-catenin binding, moves toward the plasma membrane, and needs full-length APC. Cells included colorectal cancer lines and the non-transformed line HCEC 1CT.

sources.title: The Roles of APC and Axin Derived from Experimental and Theoretical Analysis of the Wnt Pathway
sources.locator: Axin at about 20 picomolar, much lower than the other major components, against APC at about 100 nanomolar; free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin rising about sixfold, from 25 to 153 nanomolar, between reference and standard stimulated states; doubling axin drops beta-catenin half-life 50 per cent while doubling GSK3beta drops it about 10 per cent. Model supported by Xenopus egg extract measurements.
sources.license: CC BY (PLoS open-access licence permitting unrestricted use with credit); facts-only use, with no source expression reused

sources.title: Evidence that fold-change, and not absolute level, of beta-catenin dictates Wnt signaling
sources.version: Volume 36, issue 5, pages 872-884; DOI 10.1016/j.molcel.2009.11.017; PubMed Central author manuscript
sources.locator: Beta-catenin fold-change held around 6 to 9 across perturbations in RKO cells while absolute post-stimulation levels ranged from roughly 30 to 1200 nanomolar; the authors state fold-change rather than final level should potentially be the precise reporter read downstream, and note this requires remembering the pre-signal level for comparison. sources.title: The Emerging Mechanisms of Wnt Secretion and Signaling in Development
sources.publisher: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
sources.locator: Wnt proteins are hydrophobic through lipid modification, making travel in aqueous space hard to explain; palmitoylation is essential for secretion; long-range action is long-debated and the exact range not known; lipoproteins, heparan sulphate proteoglycans, exosomes and cytonemes are proposed routes; oligomerisation is argued against because blocking GFP-labelled Wingless movement did not affect Myc-labelled Wingless spreading; Wnt3 in mouse crypts shows short-range lateral transcytosis.

sources.title: Beyond the French Flag Model: Exploiting Spatial and Gene Regulatory Interactions for Positional Information
sources.locator: A morphogen gradient described as a chemical coordinate system with genes activating at different thresholds; the position-to-cue mapping can be noisy or ambiguous; one gene reading a threshold with a monotonous response function achieves at most one bit, distinguishing two regions; the four primary gap genes are estimated at 4.2 plus or minus 0.05 bits, placing a nucleus to roughly 1 per cent precision; cells need gene interaction and spatial coupling, not thresholds alone.

sources.title: Fundamental Limits to Position Determination by Concentration Gradients
sources.locator: Positional width scales as averaging time to the power minus one half, so precision improves with the square root of averaging duration; averaging about a minute can give excellent precision with only a few hundred protein copies; two-gradient systems scale more slowly at minus one quarter; biochemical noise strongly constrains subcellular positioning. The models treat positioning inside a single cell.
sources.license: CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution License permitting unrestricted use, distribution and reproduction with credit); facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the square-root scaling of positional precision with averaging time and the statement about a minute of averaging with a few hundred protein copies. No wording, equation derivation, figure, table, or dataset was copied or adapted. The lesson states in a scoping callout that the study models subcellular positioning rather than a tissue-scale gradient, and that only the structure of the argument and the scaling transfer to the crypt. The consequence that halving positional uncertainty costs four times the averaging time is this lesson's arithmetic on the source's scaling law.

sources.title: General Principles of Cell Communication
sources.publisher: Garland Science; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
sources.version: Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition; NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK26813
sources.locator: A relay chain with multiple amplification steps is often called a signaling cascade; an extracellular signal molecule binding a receptor is a ligand; cell-surface receptors act as signal transducers converting a ligand-binding event into intracellular signals that alter target-cell behaviour; what happens when a signal is withdrawn matters, its effect transitory because the signal alters unstable molecules under continual turnover; graded versus threshold responses.

sources.title: Understanding How Wnt Influences Destruction Complex Activity and beta-Catenin Dynamics
sources.locator: Two proposed mechanisms of Wnt-mediated inhibition: inactivation-by-saturation of the complex with GSK3-phosphorylated beta-catenin, and release of YAP/TAZ preventing E3 ligase docking; relocalisation of only some complexes to the membrane, with residual activity coming mainly from non-membrane complexes that stay active in the cytoplasm; the question called controversial; and a large stable pool of beta-catenin bound to E-cadherin, outside canonical Wnt signalling, removed before analysis.
